security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD's APLIC driver writes to aclicsourcecfg[0] via xiselect=0x1000/xireg2 (XLEN=32) or acliciprio[0] to configure interrupt source #0 or target #0, and subsequently assumes the write succeeded — but the hardware silently drops the write because sourcecfg[0] and target[0] are hardwired read-only zero across all APLIC domains.
security_spec.summary: Kernel that writes to aclicsourcecfg[0] or target[0] iprio fields believing it configures interrupt #0 will silently get ROZ behavior, leaving IRQ #0 effectively dead/unroutable without the kernel realizing the misconfiguration.

findings.finding: Missing lower-bound check on daf->cells[0]: only validates cells[0] > sc->ndev, but does not reject cells[0] == 0. If a malformed device tree maps interrupt source 0, subsequent calls to aplic_setup_intr/aplic_bind_intr will compute APLIC_SRC_CFG(0) = domaincfg offset (0x0000) and APLIC_TARGET(0) = genmsi offset (0x3000) via the (idx-1)*4 macro, corrupting domain configuration and MSI generation registers.

spec_citations.excerpt: APLIC domains do not implement target[0]. When accessing acliciprio[0], the bits corresponding to target[0] are read-only zero.
Indirect access to aclicsourcecfg[k] mirrors sourcecfg[k*2][15:0] up to sourcecfg[k*2+1][15:0]. Access to aclicsourcecfg[0][15:0] is read-only zero.

findings.finding: No bounds validation on irqid before accessing aplic->irqs[irqid]. A caller passing irqid == 0 or irqid >= nirqs would trigger out-of-bounds array access. While vm_assert_irq/vm_deassert_irq are the only callers, the irq parameter comes from userspace (bhyve) without validation in this function. If irqid == 0, the sourcecfg default (INACTIVE) prevents functional harm, but the OOB risk for irqid >= nirqs is real.

spec_citations.excerpt: Access to aclicsourcecfg[0][15:0] is read-only zero.

findings.finding: Interrupt initialization loop correctly starts at irq=1, skipping the non-existent interrupt source 0. APLIC_SRC_CFG(irq) with irq >= 1 always computes valid offsets. No writable aclicsourcecfg[0] or acliciprio[0] access exists in this driver.

MMIO range checks for both sourcecfg and target register windows start at index 1 (APLIC_SOURCECFG(1) and APLIC_TARGET(1)), correctly preventing guest access to the non-existent sourcecfg[0] and target[0] registers. The aplic_handle_sourcecfg function additionally rejects i <= 0.

spec_citations.excerpt: APLIC domains do not implement target[0]. When accessing acliciprio[0], the bits corresponding to target[0] are read-only zero.

findings.finding: Explicitly rejects index i <= 0 with ENOENT, enforcing that sourcecfg[0] cannot be read or written through the virtual APLIC interface.
